title: TAGRPO: Boosting GRPO on Image-to-Video Generation with Direct Trajectory Alignment
claim: Our method converges faster and reaches consistently higher reward than the strongest baseline across multiple models and reward metrics.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, left-to-right, endpoint stars with bold value labels
description: Two side-by-side line charts plot reward against training time in GPU hours, from 0 to about 1400. The left chart uses the Q-Save reward and the right chart uses HPSv3. Each chart has four curves: TAGRPO and DanceGRPO, each on two video models, Wan 2.2 and HunyuanVideo-1.5. TAGRPO curves are solid, in saturated crimson and dark maroon with round markers. DanceGRPO curves are dashed and grey with square markers. Every curve ends in a star with a bold or grey label giving the final value, for example TAGRPO (Wan 2.2) at 9.11 against DanceGRPO at 9.03, and 3.51 against 2.56 on the right. The TAGRPO curves climb steadily and pull away from the flat or declining grey baselines. A legend sits inside each plot. The eye goes first to the bold crimson endpoint labels at the top right of each chart.
caption: Performance of the proposed TAGRPO. We mainly compared our method with DanceGRPO [ref], as existing open‑sourced implementations of visual GRPO methods [ref] typically support text‑conditioned tasks, with DanceGRPO being the only exception. The results demonstrate that TAGRPO achieved faster convergence and consistently higher reward gains on both Wan 2.2 [ref] and HunyuanVideo-1.5 [ref]. We used Q‑Save [ref] and HPSv3 [ref] as reward models, and all reported reward values were averaged over the evaluation set.
abstract: Recent studies have demonstrated the efficacy of integrating Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) into flow matching models, particularly for text-to-image and text-to-video generation. However, we find that directly applying these techniques to image-to-video (I2V) models often fails to yield consistent reward improvements. To address this limitation, we present TAGRPO, a robust post-training framework for I2V models inspired by contrastive learning. Our approach is grounded in the observation that rollout videos generated from identical initial noise provide superior guidance for optimization. Leveraging this insight, we propose a novel GRPO loss applied to intermediate latents, encouraging direct alignment with high-reward trajectories while maximizing distance from low-reward counterparts. Furthermore, we introduce a memory bank for rollout videos to enhance diversity and reduce computational overhead. Despite its simplicity, TAGRPO achieves significant improvements over DanceGRPO in I2V generation. The deliverables will be updated at https://tagrpo.github.io/ .
